lessons.title: Astro 5 from zero
lessons.description: Build an Astro application while learning server islands, view transitions and the component model.
lessons.notes:
# Astro 5

Astro renders content on the server by default and lets you opt individual components into client-side interactivity.

## Key ideas

- Ship HTML by default.
- Use client directives only where interaction requires JavaScript.
- Server islands defer dynamic server-rendered sections independently.
- View transitions can preserve context between navigations.

## Before moving on

For each interactive element in your exercise, explain why it needs client-side JavaScript.

quiz.question: What does Astro ship by default for a non-interactive component?
quiz.explanation: Astro renders components to HTML and only hydrates explicitly interactive islands.

quiz.question: Why use a client directive?
options: To opt an interactive component into hydration
quiz.explanation: Client directives tell Astro when an interactive island should load and hydrate.

flashcards.back: An independently interactive component inside mostly static HTML.
An Astro instruction that controls when a client component becomes interactive.
A dynamic server-rendered region that can load independently from the surrounding page.

lessons.exercise: Build a content page with one interactive island and a view transition between two routes.
